title: The Numbered Understory That Never Reaches Zero

features.name: the counting spiral
features.desc-on-touch: Numbers carved backward into the earth, spiraling deeper. The sequence never completes—each ring reveals an older, longer count, as though the orchard was always larger than it knew.

features.name: the ledger roots
features.desc-on-touch: Where bark and paper become the same thing. Root-thick pages, numbered lines that shift when not read directly, ink that tastes like soil.

features.name: the echo that counts itself
features.desc-on-touch: A voice in the soil, numbering the dark. It has been counting so long that it has forgotten what it was counting, and began counting the forgetting itself.

features.name: the stone that keeps the place
features.desc-on-touch: A burl of stone, smooth from the hands of counters. You run your fingers down it and feel the marks of fingers that have counted the same stone so many times it has learned to count itself.

features.name: the numbering air
features.desc-on-touch: The darkness itself is numbered. Not in sequence—in depth. The deeper you descend, the older the numbers become, and the counting echoes upward from a root system that will never be fully mapped.

inscription: the numbering continues, older and slower, toward a zero that will never arrive

file.name: Orchard_Enumeration_1947-Ongoing.mp3
file.note: A field recording of counting voices from the orchard soil, played backward, forward, then in the third direction nobody teaches. The numbering has started to include trees that fell centuries ago.

reverie.title: REVERIE — afternoon, the orchard, the counting
narr: she stood in the rows and called the numbers aloud.
you moved through the trees, placing stones where she
had passed, a counter's counter, each stone a mark.
neither of you would see the same orchard twice.
the counting continued after you left. still does.
